Subject: Dedicated capacity + burst: sizing and add-on pricing

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightAsk is excited by Redwood's latency profile. We have a couple of follow-ups from our infra and procurement teams attached (BrightAsk_Summary_v2.pdf). High-level ask below: 

- Baseline: we expect steady-state inference equivalent to ~8 A100-class GPUs (peak concurrency ~320 requests/sec with avg sequence length 256).
- Peaks: traffic spikes driven by nightly batch jobs and marketing campaigns — short bursts (10–30 mins) where we could need 2–4 extra GPUs.
- Questions: how does your Dedicated burst add-on work end-to-end? Cooldown windows, per-minute billing, per-burst caps, and any spend caps you can offer? Also curious about committed-commit discounts for annual vs. monthly reserved commits.

Can you share an initial pricing sketch and a couple of packaging options (prepaid burst credits vs. per-minute top-up)? Procurement will want clear worst-case spend scenarios.

Best,
Amelia Torres

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst: sizing, cooldowns, and add-on pricing

Amelia — great notes, thanks for the clear traffic breakdown. I took a first pass at two packaging options and attached a worksheet (RDW-Dedicated-quote-20260830.xlsx). Key points up front: 

Option A — Reserved commit + per-minute burst top-up
- Reserved commit: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (annual). 10% commit discount on base Dedicated monthly rate.
- Burst: on-demand surge to +4 GPUs (max cap) for up to 30 minutes per burst. Pricing is $35 per GPU-hour for surge time, billed to the nearest minute.
- Cooldown: a 90-minute cooldown applies after a burst that exceeded 15 minutes (prevents repeated short bursts in quick succession).
- Daily cap: we can set an optional daily surge cap (e.g., $2,000/day) to limit exposure.

Option B — Reserved commit + prepaid burst credits ("burst insurance")
- Reserved commit: same as above, 8 GPUs annual commit, 8% commit discount with prepaid annual payment.
- Burst insurance: upfront pool of credits (example: 100 GPU-hours of surge) sold at an effective $22 per GPU-hour and consumed per-minute. Once credits exhaust, fallback to on-demand surge rate ($35/ GPU-hour).
- Cooldown: reduced to 60 minutes when using burst credit consumption (we accept slightly higher frequency if you prepay).
- Carryover: unused credits expire at year-end.

Tradeoffs and next steps:
- Option A gives predictability on base cost and pay-as-you-go surge but has higher marginal surge price.
- Option B lowers marginal surge cost and softens the impact of unexpected daily peaks but requires upfront cash (typical for finance teams).

If you can share an expected monthly distribution of peak minutes (or 7-day sample), we can model exact worst-case spend under each option. I linked the HubSpot deal in the attached worksheet.

Attaching the worksheet and a short scenario table. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement + infra to walk the numbers.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the quick reply and the two options. A few procurement clarifications before we loop legal: 

1) The cooldown language: can you make it deterministic? We need an explicit cooldown per burst length (example: burst <=15m => 30m cooldown; 15–30m => 90m cooldown; >30m => 180m cooldown). The phrasing "reduced to 60 minutes" for prepaid credits is helpful — we need exact numbers to include in the SOW.

2) Daily spend cap: we'd like a hard cap option (not just optional) that prevents charges above X/day without explicit sign-off from our finance contact. Can Redwood implement an automatic throttle/fail-open once the daily surge cap is hit?

3) Prepaid credits: what happens with prepayment if we decommission early? Any pro-rata refund or credit transfer rules?

4) Could you provide a worst-case monthly spend example for both options assuming: baseline 8 GPUs always on, and 80 minutes/day of +4 GPUs (in three 25–30 minute bursts)?

Procurement will also want a short clause for emergency top-ups (manual approval path + flat expedite fee).

Appreciate it — will schedule a short call when we have the numbers.

Regards,
Procurement Team
BrightAsk

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity + burst: pricing clarifications (internal)

Jonas — quick internal note before we respond to procurement:

- Cooldown tiers: we can offer deterministic tiers as requested (<=15m => 30m; 15–30m => 90m; >30m => 180m) for both options. For prepaid credits, drop the 90m to 60m only for bursts that consume credits; >30m remains 180m.
- Daily hard cap: technically feasible, but it ties into throttling behavior. We can implement an auto-throttle that returns 429s once the cap is reached; if customer wants fail-open (allow but invoice), that's the default today. For a hard cap + auto-throttle we need a small product change and a 6-week SLA to ship it.
- Refunds on prepayment: standard policy — pro-rata refund on unused credits with a 30-day processing fee (or transfer to another Redwood account if you list the target). Finance prefers transfer to avoid refunds.

Proposed counter: offer prepaid burst credits at $20/GPU-hour for a 100-hour pool (effective ~43% off on-demand surge), 60-minute cooldown on credit-eligible bursts, and provide an optional hard daily cap implementation with a 6-week delivery timeline. In return, ask for the 8 GPU annual commit with 9% overall commit discount (blended).

I'm attaching a quick scenario CSV showing margin impact at $20 vs $22. If you want to be aggressive, we can hold $18 for a multi-year commit.

Priyom
Head of Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Amelia / Procurement — thanks for the clear asks. Per Priyom's note, here's the updated, formal proposal & next steps: 

Summary (final):
- Baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, annual commit.
- Commit discount: 9% blended on base Dedicated rate (annual prepay).
- Burst insurance: 100 GPU-hours prepaid pool at $20/GPU-hour (consumes per-minute).
- On-demand surge fallback: $35/GPU-hour.
- Cooldown tiers (deterministic): <=15m burst => 30m cooldown; 15–30m => 90m; >30m => 180m. For bursts consuming prepaid credits, the 15–30m tier cooldown becomes 60m.
- Hard daily cap: available as an add-on (auto-throttle -> 429 responses) delivered in 6 weeks; we will ship a toggle in Console and a webhook to notify when cap triggers.
- Emergency top-up: manual approval path via Account team + flat expedite fee of $150 per top-up request.

Worst-case example (monthly) — your scenario (80 min/day at +4 GPUs):
- Extra GPU-hours per month: (80 minutes/day * 30 days) => 40 GPU-hours/day? Wait compute: 80 min/day * 30 = 2400 min => 40 GPU-hours/day? That's incorrect in-line. See attached worksheet for clean math.
- Attached worksheet contains modeled monthly charges under Option B and a conservative worst-case where you exhaust prepaid credits and rely on on-demand surge.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, I'll send the SOW + DocuSign link for signature (DocuSign link included below).
2) For the hard daily cap, confirm whether you want throttle (auto-429) or fail-open with invoice; we need this choice to scope the SOW for the 6-week delivery.
3) Send your finance contact if you want the prepaid invoice to be directed to someone else.
